A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDM research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison; v1 Appendices A–D correspond to v2 supplementary Sections 7–10.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, a 1,008-sample human-preference study, formula-style perturbation experiments, and appendix experiments on training-data selection.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies, revises reported evaluation results, and adds results for three updated UniMERNet configurations in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces repeated rendering of one black token against gray tokens with distinct RGB colors for individual tokens and localization by color extraction. This changes the localization procedure, while Hungarian matching, invalid-match elimination, and metric calculation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four UniMER-Test subsets, Tiny-Doc-Math formula-level and document-level tasks, UniMER-1M data-selection experiment, and formula-style perturbations. Table 4 adds model configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The alternative evaluation metrics and recognition algorithms in the matched comparisons remain unchanged. Table 4 extends UniMERNet checkpoint and size configurations, without introducing a distinct comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: New supplementary Section 11 and Table 4 evaluate updated UniMERNet-tiny, small, and base weights using per-subset CDM and ExpRate@CDM. Existing dataset sizes, the 1,008-sample human study, style-perturbation design, and document-matching thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The style-robustness experiment, human-preference cases, model-error analyses, hard-case data selection, and image-difference examples are retained. Figure 8 updates numerical distributions within the existing analysis; Table 4 supplies additional benchmark results without a new ablation or diagnostic question.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based variability estimates. Human-study sample counts and randomization descriptions remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, rendering-success rates, and Figure 8 contain substantial result revisions. For example, Table 1 changes Mathpix CDM from 0.896 to 0.951 and reverses its ExpRate@CDM ordering relative to Texify; Table 3 changes Nougat document-level CDM from 0.7838 to 0.8326. Table 4 adds updated UniMERNet configuration results. The PDFs do not fully explain the causes of these revisions.

T1.justification: The matching objective, three matching-cost definitions, affine-transformation assumption, and CDM/ExpRate@CDM formulas remain mathematically equivalent. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that spatial character matching provides a fairer, more intuitive formula-recognition evaluation than text-based metrics and aligns closely with human judgment. The revised title and conclusion wording do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning representation-style bias, GPT-4o hallucinations, Mathpix punctuation omissions, and Nougat failures remain unchanged. Both versions also acknowledge rendering failures and character-style ambiguity as CDM limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a CDM code-access link in the abstract and specifies the RGB interval of 15, token-color assignment command, and color-based localization. Existing appendix preprocessing instructions and matching thresholds are retained; no new hardware or training-budget information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds background citations including M6Doc, DocBank, Image2Struct, MinerU, and TextHawk2. These broaden contextual references without substantially changing CDM's positioning against text-based and image-difference metrics.

P1.justification: The title and author line change, introductory prose receives local edits, experimental subheadings gain numbering, and appendices become numbered supplementary sections. Most paragraphs and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 revises its localization panel, Figures 3–4 receive visual redesigns, Figure 5 moves from the appendix into the main text, and Table 4 is added. Typography and placement change, while most existing displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful implementation information and model-configuration results, but numerical consistency worsens. For example, Table 3 revises formula-level GPT-4o CDM from 0.7120 to 0.7330 while Figure 8 retains 0.712; Section 7.1 also retains old failure rates despite updated success rates in Section 5.2.1. The unexplained result revisions and unresolved discrepancies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
